assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into programmable recruiters of the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery, a clear molecular design principle for rewiring cellular proteins. It extends drug action to targets once considered undruggable and has changed what chemists and clinicians can attempt, with a large tool and drug-discovery community.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies are central to the PROTAC concept and its first demonstrations, and Ciulli to structure-guided design and VHL-based degraders. The molecular-glue arm (thalidomide-cereblon work by Handa, Ito and others) is a distinct lineage, so a three-person prize cannot cover everything. I would honour the PROTAC core and accept that glue degraders are partially left out.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of work with independent confirmation across many labs and several degraders in clinical trials. Interpretation is stable. Clinical proof of benefit is still maturing, but the chemistry is established and recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Whether clinical approval is needed before recognition; my recollection of trial status is not verified.
Allocation between PROTACs and molecular glues, and the early contributions of Sakamoto, Kim and Handa/Ito.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved the delivery problem for siRNA and mRNA medicines, a chemistry of lipid pKa, self-assembly and endosomal escape. Its effect on what clinicians can do is very large, as seen in patisiran and the mRNA vaccines, and it is the kind of molecular-materials design that reaches patients.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope are credited with the foundational lipid-nanoparticle formation and ionizable-lipid concepts, and Anderson with combinatorial lipid discovery and later delivery systems. Madden, MacLachlan and Langer are also plausible. Credit is spread across several groups and companies, making a three-person configuration contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly validated by approved products and billions of vaccine doses, with broad independent confirmation. Recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modifications may make the committee cautious about overlap.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize.
Fair allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved, and I cannot verify exact priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing performs targeted chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks, a deliberate application of nucleoside chemistry and protein engineering to the genome. It is a precise, general tool with therapeutic consequences, and the first clinical results are encouraging.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead first authors of the cytosine and adenine editors. Kondo and Nishida had an independent related deaminase-based approach. A sole-laureate or Liu-led configuration is fair, though trainee credit is sometimes recognised.
assessment.maturity: Adopted widely since 2016 with many independent replications and clinical translation under way. Not yet fully matured therapeutically, and the 2020 chemistry prize for CRISPR-Cas9 makes the timing question sensitive.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will consider genome editing already recognised in 2020.
Treatment of Kondo and Nishida's independent work and of the lead trainees.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, giving chemical control over proteins in living systems. It has widespread use in protein engineering, imaging, bioorthogonal labelling and biotherapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues, including Lei Wang, established the first orthogonal pairs and site-specific incorporation in E. coli and then eukaryotes. Chin extended the approach to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and genome-scale recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also made important contributions. Allocation is manageable but not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent validation and general use. Mature, with enduring influence, though it is a platform whose largest payoffs are still arriving.
uncertainties: Weighting of Chin's later genomic recoding relative to the original Schultz-lab discovery.
Whether the 2022 bioorthogonal chemistry prize reduces the committee's appetite for this neighbouring area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically and underlies portable long-read DNA and RNA sequencing. It is a striking union of protein engineering, single-molecule biophysics and analytical chemistry, with direct consequences for biology and clinical diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Church-linked early concepts, Kasianowicz's alpha-hemolysin demonstration, Bayley's engineered pores and Akeson's enzyme-controlled translocation all matter. The attribution is genuinely complex and no three-person subset captures it cleanly.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercial and widely confirmed, and chemically modified or engineered pores keep improving. Timing is reasonable, though the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson are contested.
The candidate list does not include some people who may be important to the engineering of commercial systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry reduced the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude. It is analytical chemistry with enormous influence on biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule array approach. Other pioneers, such as Mayer, Ju and Rothberg, developed related platforms. The two Cambridge chemists make a clean core pair, but the field has several technology lineages.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and globally adopted. Very strong confirmation and timing is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views sequencing as chemistry or as biology/medicine.
Competing platform claims could complicate who is honoured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids give designable recognition and assembly between nanomaterials and biomolecules, with applications in diagnostics, gene regulation and materials. It is close to my own area of peptide- and DNA-directed nanoparticle assembly.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group is the dominant source of the DNA-gold nanoparticle concept, with Alivisatos's contemporaneous independent work on DNA-nanocrystal assembly. Credit for the spherical nucleic acid idea appears to rest mainly with Mirkin.
assessment.maturity: Concept confirmed widely in nanoscience, but clinical and commercial impact remains moderate, and some biological uses are still developing.
uncertainties: Real-world impact is smaller than for the highest-ranked candidates.
Alivisatos may be considered more for quantum dots than for DNA assembly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant via the switch-II pocket showed that a notorious oncogene can be drugged, and his earlier chemical-genetic analog-sensitive kinase approach is a general chemical biology tool. The work is a clear example of chemistry changing clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is clearly the intellectual originator of the KRAS G12C covalent strategy and the analog-sensitive kinase approach. Sotorasib and adagrasib were developed by companies building on this, so a sole-laureate prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Clinical approvals and numerous follow-on inhibitors give strong validation. Durability of response and resistance are still being understood, so the clinical story is not yet closed.
uncertainties: Weight of company drug development relative to the academic discovery.
Whether the committee prefers a single-laureate prize for a medicinal chemistry story.
